review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Ἀρχόμεθα πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνειν; ἢ μὴ χρῄζομεν ὥς τινες συστατικῶν ἐπιστολῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐξ ὑμῶν;
3:1.targetText: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

unmappedSource.reason: μή marks a question expecting the answer no; BSB has no separate word for it.

3:2.sourceText: ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν ὑμεῖς ἐστε, ἐνγεγραμμένη ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν, γινωσκομένη καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων,
3:2.targetText: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

groups.note: πάντων ἀνθρώπων ("all people") is rendered everyone.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:3.sourceText: φανερούμενοι ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφ’ ἡμῶν, ἐνγεγραμμένη οὐ μέλανι ἀλλὰ Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ζῶντος, οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν λιθίναις ἀλλ’ ἐν πλαξὶν καρδίαις σαρκίναις.
3:3.targetText: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

groups.note: The participle φανερούμενοι ("being shown") is rendered is clear.
The participle διακονηθεῖσα ("ministered") is rendered the result of … ministry.
ὑφ’ ἡμῶν ("by us") is rendered our.
σαρκίναις ("of flesh") is rendered human.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an impersonal subject; the participle refers to the readers.

3:4.sourceText: Πεποίθησιν δὲ τοιαύτην ἔχομεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.
3:4.targetText: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.

groups.note: ἔχομεν ("we have") is rendered is ours.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:5.sourceText: οὐχ ὅτι ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν λογίσασθαί τι ὡς ἐξ ἑαυτῶν, ἀλλ’ ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ,
3:5.targetText: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.

groups.note: ἀπό ("from") is rendered in.
ὡς ("as") introduces what is claimed, rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.

3:6.sourceText: ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης, οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος· τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ.
3:6.targetText: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

groups.note: Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

3:7.sourceText: Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν γράμμασιν ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον Μωϋσέως διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν καταργουμένην,
3:7.targetText: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,

groups.note: ὥστε ("so that") is rendered such … that.
υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ ("sons of Israel") is rendered Israelites.
προσώπου αὐτοῦ ("of his face") is rendered its, referring to the face.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:8.sourceText: πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἡ διακονία τοῦ πνεύματος ἔσται ἐν δόξῃ;
3:8.targetText: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?

groups.note: ἐν δόξῃ ("in glory") is rendered glorious.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the question "how will … not" without a word for πῶς ("how").

3:9.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἡ διακονία τῆς κατακρίσεως δόξα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον περισσεύει ἡ διακονία τῆς δικαιοσύνης δόξῃ.
3:9.targetText: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this article; "the" still renders it.
δόξα ("glory") is rendered glorious.
περισσεύει … δόξῃ ("abounds in glory") is rendered glorious … is.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

3:10.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ οὐ δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει εἵνεκεν τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης δόξης.
3:10.targetText: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered Indeed.
δεδόξασται ("has been glorified") is rendered has … glory.
ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει εἵνεκεν ("in this respect, because of") is rendered in comparison to.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an adverb marking the former state.
English adds an adverb; the Greek has none.

3:11.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ τὸ καταργούμενον διὰ δόξης, πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ μένον ἐν δόξῃ.
3:11.targetText: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!

groups.note: μᾶλλον ("more") is rendered greater.
ἐν δόξῃ ("in glory") is rendered the glory of.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

3:12.sourceText: Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα πολλῇ παρρησίᾳ χρώμεθα,
3:12.targetText: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.

groups.note: χρώμεθα παρρησίᾳ ("we use boldness") is rendered we are … bold.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle Ἔχοντες ("having").

3:13.sourceText: καὶ οὐ καθάπερ Μωϋσῆς ἐτίθει κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου.
3:13.targetText: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.

groups.note: πρὸς τό with the infinitive gives the purpose.
The negative μή ("not") is rendered keep … from.
υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ ("sons of Israel") is rendered Israelites.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek leaves them understood.

3:14.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει, μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται·
3:14.targetText: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.

groups.note: σήμερον ("today") with ἡμέρας is rendered this day.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἀνακαλυπτόμενον ("being unveiled").
English adds an adverb; the Greek has none.

3:15.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἕως σήμερον ἡνίκα ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται Μωϋσῆς κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν κεῖται·
3:15.targetText: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.

groups.note: ἀλλά ("but") is rendered And.
κεῖται ἐπί ("lies on") is rendered covers.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds even for emphasis; the Greek connective is only ἀλλά ("but"), with no καί.

3:16.sourceText: ἡνίκα δὲ ἐὰν ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς Κύριον, περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα.
3:16.targetText: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

3:17.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Κύριος τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστιν· οὗ δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα Κυρίου, ἐλευθερία.
3:17.targetText: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English adds there is to answer where; the Greek has no ἐκεῖ ("there") and no verb.

3:18.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν, καθάπερ ἀπὸ Κυρίου Πνεύματος.
3:18.targetText: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

groups.note: ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν ("from glory to glory") is rendered with intensifying glory.

unmappedSource.reason: τὴν αὐτήν ("the same") has no English counterpart; BSB says His image instead of the same image.
καθάπερ ("just as") is not rendered; BSB recasts the phrase as a relative clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB names the image as the Lord's; the Greek says "the same".
English supplies a relative clause; the Greek has no verb.
English turns the apposition "the Lord, the Spirit" into a relative clause.
